passage: When the Riverside Middle School garden club started, its members planted only tomatoes and beans. Over five years, they added fruit trees, a greenhouse, and a compost system that turns cafeteria scraps into soil. Today the garden supplies vegetables to the school kitchen several times a week, and science teachers use it for lessons on plant growth and soil health.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Over time, a small school garden became a resource for the kitchen and science classes.
The garden club spent five years trying to grow fruit trees but could not keep them alive.
Science teachers created the school garden so that students could study how plants grow.
The cafeteria stopped using vegetables from the garden once the compost system was built.
steps: The text traces change over time: from two crops to fruit trees, a greenhouse and compost.
It ends with the result: the garden supplies the kitchen and supports science lessons.
The main idea combines that growth with what the garden now provides.
The text never says the trees failed, says the club (not teachers) started it, and says the garden still supplies the kitchen.
key: For a main idea, connect the beginning of the text to where it ends up.
